blocks.content: Life originated approximately 3.5 billion years ago. Over geological time, species diversified due to environmental changes, continental drift, climatic shifts, and ecological interactions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Life originated approximately 3.5 billion years ago and diversified due to geological, climatic, and ecological factors.
Speciation is driven by reproductive isolation, whereas natural selection preserves organisms best adapted to survive.
Mutations act as the fundamental source of genetic variation, while genetic drift causes random changes in small populations.
Earth has experienced five historical mass extinctions, with human activities currently driving a potential sixth mass extinction.

blocks.content: Scientists warn that human-driven biodiversity loss may represent the Sixth Mass Extinction.
• Speciation – formation of new species due to reproductive isolation.
• Natural Selection – organisms best adapted survive and reproduce.

items: Mutation is frequently tested as the single primary source of all genetic variation.
Genetic Drift specifically affects small populations through random genetic shifts.
Speciation requires reproductive isolation to form distinct new species.
Adaptive Radiation describes the diversification of a single ancestral lineage into multiple ecological forms.

blocks.content: • Adaptive Radiation – diversification of a single ancestral species into many forms.
